projects.title: Complete TimSort Pipeline Architecture (Run Identification + Binary Insertion + Galloping Merge)
projects.description: TimSort (used in Python and Java standard libraries) is an adaptive hybrid sorting algorithm derived from Merge Sort and Insertion Sort. 1) Identifies natural ascending/descending runs; 2) Extends short runs to `minrun` using Binary Insertion Sort; 3) Merges runs using Galloping Mode in `O(N log N)` worst case and `O(N)` linear best case! In this project, you will build Complete TimSort Pipeline in C.
projects.learningOutcome: TimSort Industrial Pipeline, Natural Run Identification & Adaptive Galloping Merges
projects.exampleText: Execute complete TimSort pipeline on real-world dataset
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Complete TimSort Pipeline Architecture ---
Partitioned array into natural runs, sorted small runs with Binary Insertion Sort, merged with Galloping Mode.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Run Identification**: Find natural sorted runs in input array; flip descending runs.
2. **Run Padding**: Pad runs `< minrun` using Binary Insertion Sort; merge runs using galloping mode.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `timsort_pipeline_demo()`: Solves complete TimSort pipeline architecture.

projects.title: Sorting Decision Matrix Engine (Selecting Best Sorter based on Data Constraints)
projects.description: Build an automated Decision Matrix Engine that selects the OPTIMAL sorting algorithm based on data properties: 1) Small arrays (`N <= 16`): Insertion Sort; 2) Known small range `0..K`: Counting Sort; 3) 32-bit Integers: Radix Sort; 4) Memory Constrained (`O(1)` RAM): HeapSort; 5) General / Nearly-Sorted: TimSort/IntroSort! In this project, you will build Decision Matrix Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Sorting Decision Matrix, Constraints Profiling (N, Range, Memory, Stability) & Optimal Selection
projects.exampleText: Select optimal sorting algorithm based on dataset constraints
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Sorting Decision Matrix Engine ---
Selected RadixSort for large 32-bit integers, InsertionSort for small N<=16, QuickSort for general data.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Constraint Evaluation**: Inspect input array size N, integer bounds, stability needs, and RAM limits.
2. **Dynamic Dispatch**: Route dataset to the fastest matching sorter.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `sorting_decision_matrix_demo()`: Solves Sorting Decision Matrix Engine.

projects.title: Bitonic Sort Kernel for Networks of Size Power of 2
projects.description: Bitonic Sort is a parallel sorting network algorithm that converts arbitrary sequences into bitonic sequences (first increasing, then decreasing), then merges them. Works on power-of-2 input sizes `N = 2^k` in `O(log^2 N)` parallel steps on GPU/hardware networks! In this project, you will build Bitonic Sort Kernel in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Bitonic Sequence Definitions, Sorting Network Comparators & Parallel O(log^2 N) Steps
projects.exampleText: Sort power-of-2 array using Bitonic Sort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Bitonic Sort Kernel for Networks of Size Power of 2 ---
Sorted power-of-2 array using parallel Bitonic Sorting Network in O(log^2 N) parallel steps.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Bitonic Sequence**: Build sequence where `x_0 <= ... <= x_k >= ... >= x_{n-1}`.
2. **Bitonic Merge**: Compare and swap pairs separated by distance `2^p`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bitonic_sort_demo()`: Solves Bitonic Sort for power-of-2 arrays.

projects.title: Pancake Sorting (Prefix Reversals Sorter)
projects.description: Pancake Sorting sorts an array using ONLY ONE operation: `flip(k)`, which reverses the order of the first `k` elements in the array (like flipping a stack of pancakes with a spatula!). Find max element, flip it to index 0, then flip it to its correct target index in `O(N^2)` time and `O(1)` space. In this project, you will build Pancake Sorter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Pancake Sorting Spatula Flips `flip(k)`, Prefix Reversals & Minimum Flip Proofs
projects.exampleText: Sort array using prefix reversals flip(k)
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Pancake Sorting (Prefix Reversals Sorter) ---
Sorted array by executing max 2*N prefix reversal flips (flip(k)).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Locate Max**: Find index of largest unsorted element `max_idx` in `0..i`.
2. **Dual Flip**: `flip(max_idx + 1)` brings max to index 0; `flip(i + 1)` brings max to index `i`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `pancake_sort_demo()`: Solves Pancake Sorting using prefix reversals.

projects.title: Cycle Sort (Optimal Minimum Memory Writes Sorter)
projects.description: Cycle Sort is an in-place UNSTABLE sorting algorithm that minimizes the number of memory writes to array elements. Performs at most `O(N)` memory writes (theoretical minimum!), making it ideal for EEPROM / Flash memory where writes wear out physical hardware! In this project, you will build Cycle Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Cycle Sort In-Place Permutations, Minimum Memory Writes & EEPROM Memory Longevity
projects.exampleText: Sort array performing theoretical minimum memory writes
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Cycle Sort (Optimal Minimum Memory Writes Sorter) ---
Sorted array with theoretical MINIMUM number of memory writes (O(N) writes max).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Cycle Counting**: Count number of smaller elements to right of `arr[i]` to find target position `pos`.
2. **Permutation Swap**: Rotate elements along cycle until element returns to start position.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `cycle_sort_demo()`: Solves Cycle Sort.

projects.title: Strand Sort for Linked Lists
projects.description: Strand Sort works exceptionally well on Singly Linked Lists. Pulls out increasing 'sub-strands' from the input list in a single pass, and merges each sub-strand into a master sorted output list in `O(N^2)` worst-case and `O(N)` best-case time! In this project, you will build Strand Sort for Linked Lists in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Strand Extraction Mechanics, Sub-Strand Merging & Linked List Data Structures
projects.exampleText: Sort linked list via Strand Sort sub-strand extractions
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Strand Sort for Linked Lists ---
Sorted linked list by pulling increasing sub-strands and merging into output list.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Extract Sub-Strand**: Traverse list; move increasing elements into `strand` list.
2. **Merge Sub-Strand**: Merge `strand` into main `output` list.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `strand_sort_demo()`: Solves Strand Sort for Linked Lists.

projects.title: Sleep Sort (Multi-Threaded Timer Sorter)
projects.description: Sleep Sort is an esoteric multi-threaded sorting algorithm where for each element `val`, a separate thread is spawned that sleeps for `val` milliseconds, then prints `val`. Elements awaken and output in sorted ascending order! In this project, you will build Multi-Threaded Sleep Sort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Multi-Threaded Concurrency, Operating System Sleep Timers & Esoteric Algorithms
projects.exampleText: Sort array using multi-threaded sleep timers
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Sleep Sort (Multi-Threaded Timer Sorter) ---
Spawned threads sleeping for element value milliseconds; outputted values in sleep order.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Spawn Thread**: Spawn POSIX thread for each value `val`.
2. **Sleep & Print**: Thread calls `usleep(val * 1000)`; prints `val` upon waking.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `sleep_sort_demo()`: Solves Sleep Sort.

projects.title: Stooge Sort (Recursive 2/3 Subarray Sorter)
projects.description: Stooge Sort is a recursive sorting algorithm with a terrible time complexity of `O(N^(log 3 / log 1.5)) = O(N^2.709)`. Swaps first and last if out of order, then recursively calls Stooge Sort on: 1) First 2/3 elements; 2) Last 2/3 elements; 3) First 2/3 elements again! In this project, you will build Stooge Sort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Stooge Sort Recurrence, Overlapping Subproblem Recursions & Complex Complexity Proofs
projects.exampleText: Sort array using 2/3 overlap Stooge Sort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Stooge Sort (Recursive 2/3 Subarray Sorter) ---
Sorted array recursively in O(N^2.7) time using 2/3 overlap swaps.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Initial Swap**: Swap `arr[low]` and `arr[high]` if out of order.
2. **3-Way 2/3 Recurse**: Recurse on `first 2/3`, `last 2/3`, and `first 2/3` again.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `stooge_sort_demo()`: Solves Stooge Sort.

projects.title: BogoSort (Stupid Random Shuffle Profiler)
projects.description: BogoSort (Shotgun Sort) repeatedly generates a random permutation of the array using Fisher-Yates shuffle until the array happens to be sorted! Expected time complexity: `O((N+1)!)`. Use as a benchmark baseline for sorting efficiency! In this project, you will build BogoSort Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Random Permutation Generation, Fisher-Yates Shuffling & Combinatorial Factorial Proofs
projects.exampleText: Shuffle array randomly until sorted via BogoSort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- BogoSort (Stupid Random Shuffle Profiler) ---
Shuffled array randomly until sorted in O((N+1)!) expected time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Sorted Test**: Check if `is_sorted(arr)` is true.
2. **Fisher-Yates Shuffle**: If not sorted, randomly shuffle array and repeat.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `bogosort_demo()`: Solves BogoSort random shuffle profiler.

projects.description: Build an Audit Matrix comparing 10 major sorting algorithms across 5 core industrial dimensions: Worst-Case Time, Best-Case Time, Auxiliary Memory, Stability, and Adaptivity. projects.logicExplanation:

projects.codeExplanation: 1. `trade_off_matrix_demo()`: Solves Sorting Algorithm Trade-Off Audit Matrix.

projects.title: IntroSort Complete Production C Implementation
projects.description: Build a complete production-grade IntroSort engine in C. Combines QuickSort partition depth limit `2 * log2(N)` with HeapSort fallback and InsertionSort cutoff `N <= 16`. Eliminates QuickSort `O(N^2)` worst-case while maintaining average QuickSort cache performance! In this project, you will build Production IntroSort in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Production IntroSort Architecture, Maximum Recursion Depth Guards & Guaranteed O(N log N)
projects.exampleText: Execute production IntroSort combining QuickSort, HeapSort, and InsertionSort
projects.exampleOutput:
--- IntroSort Complete Production C Implementation ---
Executed hybrid QuickSort + HeapSort + InsertionSort engine.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **QuickSort Main**: Partition array using Median-of-Three pivot.
2. **HeapSort Fallback**: If depth limit reaches 0, switch to HeapSort; if `N <= 16`, run InsertionSort.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `introsort_production_demo()`: Solves IntroSort Complete Production C Implementation.

projects.title: TimSort Galloping Mode Optimization
projects.description: Implement TimSort's Galloping Mode: during merge phase, if run A wins 7 times in a row (`min_gallop = 7`), switch to exponential binary search (galloping) to find insertion positions in `O(log K)` time instead of linear element-by-element comparisons! In this project, you will build TimSort Galloping Mode in C.
projects.learningOutcome: TimSort Galloping Mode, Exponential Binary Search & Subarray Merge Acceleration
projects.exampleText: Activate galloping mode when 7 consecutive wins occur in run A
projects.exampleOutput:
--- TimSort Galloping Mode Optimization ---
Activated exponential binary search galloping mode when 7 consecutive wins occurred in run A.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Consecutive Win Count**: Track consecutive wins from run A or run B.
2. **Gallop Binary Search**: Execute exponential binary search `1, 2, 4, 8...` to find cut index.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `timsort_galloping_demo()`: Solves TimSort Galloping Mode Optimization.

projects.title: Batcher's Odd-Even Merge Sorting Network Engine
projects.description: Batcher's Odd-Even Merge Sort is a parallel sorting network designed for hardware circuits and GPUs. Merges two sorted lists by recursively merging odd-indexed and even-indexed sub-lists, then applying compare-and-swap on adjacent elements in `O(log^2 N)` parallel steps! In this project, you will build Batcher's Sorting Network in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Batcher's Odd-Even Merge Networks, Fixed Hardware Comparators & Parallel GPU Passes
projects.exampleText: Execute Batcher's Odd-Even Merge Sorting Network
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Batcher's Odd-Even Merge Sorting Network Engine ---
Executed fixed comparator network sorting pass in O(log^2 N) stages.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Odd-Even Sub-Merges**: Merge odd-indexed elements and even-indexed elements separately.
2. **Adjacent Comparators**: Perform `compare_swap(i, i+1)` for `i = 1, 3, 5...`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `batcher_sorting_network_demo()`: Solves Batcher's Odd-Even Merge Sorting Network Engine.

projects.title: In-Place Cycle Sorting for Custom Index Permutations
projects.description: Permute an array according to a given target index map `target_idx[i]` in-place in `O(N)` time using Cycle Sorting without extra array memory. Follows permutation cycles to swap elements directly into their target positions! In this project, you will build In-Place Index Permutation Sorter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: In-Place Index Permutations, Permutation Cycle Following & Zero Auxiliary RAM
projects.exampleText: Permute array according to custom index map in-place
projects.exampleOutput:
--- In-Place Cycle Sorting for Custom Index Permutations ---
Permuted array elements in-place to target index map in O(N) memory writes.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Cycle Traversal**: Follow permutation chain `i -> target_idx[i] -> ...`.
2. **In-Place Swap**: Swap element to correct target index until cycle closes.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `cycle_sort_permutation_demo()`: Solves In-Place Cycle Sorting for Custom Index Permutations.

projects.title: Multi-Column Database Table Multi-Key Sorting
projects.description: Sort a multi-column database table across multiple keys (e.g. `Department ASC`, `Salary DESC`, `Age ASC`). Demonstrate why STABLE sorting algorithms (MergeSort/TimSort) enable multi-pass multi-key sorting by sorting from LEAST significant key to MOST significant key! In this project, you will build Multi-Key Table Sorter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Multi-Key Database Table Sorting, Stable Multi-Pass Invariants & Column Comparators
projects.exampleText: Sort database table across multiple key columns stably
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Multi-Column Database Table Multi-Key Sorting ---
Executed stable multi-pass sorting over (Department ASC, Salary DESC, Age ASC).
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Multi-Pass Stability**: Sort by `Age` first, then `Salary`, then `Department` using a stable sorter.
2. **Preserved Order**: Stability preserves relative ordering of equal keys from previous passes.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `multi_column_db_sort_demo()`: Solves Multi-Column Database Table Multi-Key Sorting.

projects.title: Memory-Efficient Hybrid Sort for Embedded Microcontrollers
projects.description: Microcontrollers (e.g. ARM Cortex-M0 / AVR ATmega328) have restricted SRAM memory (e.g. 2 KB). Build a memory-efficient hybrid sorter combining HeapSort (in-place `O(1)` memory) and InsertionSort (`N <= 16`) that operates inside a tiny 512-byte SRAM stack budget! In this project, you will build Embedded Hybrid Sorter in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Embedded Systems Memory Budgets, SRAM Footprint Minimization & Microcontroller Sorters
projects.exampleText: Sort data operating inside 512-byte SRAM microcontroller stack budget
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Memory-Efficient Hybrid Sort for Embedded Microcontrollers ---
Executed HeapSort + InsertionSort engine operating inside 512 bytes SRAM.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **HeapSort Core**: Use HeapSort to guarantee `O(1)` RAM usage.
2. **Insertion Cutoff**: Switch to InsertionSort for `N <= 16` to leverage L1 cache locality.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `embedded_hybrid_sort_demo()`: Solves Memory-Efficient Hybrid Sort for Embedded Microcontrollers.

projects.title: Sorting Nearly-Sorted K-Sorted Arrays (Displaced by at most K positions)
projects.description: Given a K-sorted array where each element is displaced by AT MOST K positions from its target sorted location, sort the array in `O(N log K)` time using a Min-Heap of size `K + 1`! In this project, you will build K-Sorted Array Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: K-Sorted Array Properties, Min-Heap Size `K+1` Sliding Window & O(N log K) Speed
projects.exampleText: Sort K-sorted array in O(N log K) time using Min-Heap of size K+1
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Sorting Nearly-Sorted K-Sorted Arrays ---
Sorted K-sorted array using Min-Heap of size K+1 in O(N log K) time.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Heap Window Size K+1**: Insert first `K+1` elements into Min-Heap.
2. **Extract & Slide**: Extract min element to output array; insert next element from input array into heap.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `k_sorted_array_demo()`: Solves Sorting Nearly-Sorted K-Sorted Arrays.

projects.title: Topological Sorting vs Comparison Sorting Decision Audit
projects.description: Compare Topological Sorting (Kahn's BFS / DFS on Directed Acyclic Graphs in `O(V + E)`) vs Comparison Sorting (`O(N log N)`). Demonstrate when data relationships demand a DAG partial ordering vs a total comparison ordering! In this project, you will build Topo vs Comparison Audit Engine in C.
projects.learningOutcome: Partial Ordering vs Total Ordering, DAG Dependency Networks & Topological Sort Audits
projects.exampleText: Audit topological partial ordering vs comparison total ordering
projects.exampleOutput:
--- Topological Sorting vs Comparison Sorting Decision Audit ---
Audited DAG dependency sorting vs comparison total ordering.
projects.logicExplanation:
1. **Total Order**: Comparison sorting orders all pairs `(u, v)`.
2. **Partial Order**: Topological sorting orders only directed edge dependencies `u -> v`.
projects.codeExplanation: 1. `topo_vs_comparison_sort_demo()`: Solves Topological Sorting vs Comparison Sorting Decision Audit.
